briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B as D.C. Circuit Locks In Rescheduling — Psilocybin's FDA Fast Lane Opens
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market just crossed $17 billion in lifetime sales even as operators route around the 24% wholesale tax through cost-sharing deals, repeal bills, and a governor's-race endorsement built on tax relief. Nationally, courts just affirmed Schedule III for medical marijuana, Trulieve landed on the NYSE, and Compass Pathways got fast-tracked by the FDA — real momentum for operators willing to move.

local.text: Michigan cannabis sales blow past $17 billion — The state's combined adult-use and medical marijuana market has now generated more than $17B lifetime, per a new CRA monthly report, throwing off an estimated $2.66 billion in state taxes.

Tax-repeal push gains political muscle — A GOP lawmaker filed House Bill 6224 to kill the 24% wholesale tax outright, and Michigan's cannabis trade group just endorsed gubernatorial candidate John James over his pledge to repeal or roll it back.
Menominee could add four new dispensary licenses — A pending petition drive would raise the city's retail cap from nine stores to 13, opening fresh licensing opportunity for operators eyeing the U.P.

Detroit Metro Times crowns Michigan's best weed brands — This year's Best of Detroit picks spotlighted Lansing-based Hey! Captain's inventive edibles and the Zalympix competition, where 100-plus blind flower and rosin submissions battle for bragging rights.

Tax squeezes closures, but suppliers are finding a fix — Higher Love shut five of nine U.P. stores citing the wholesale tax as active licenses statewide slipped from 845 to 836, while rival Rize kept growing by splitting the tax burden with suppliers instead of absorbing it alone.

national.text: Compass Pathways gets FDA fast lane for psilocybin — The FDA granted Compass a rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for COMP360 psilocybin in treatment-resistant depression, compressing the path to a potential approval.

Federal court locks in medical marijuana's Schedule III status — The D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge to April's rescheduling order on Sept. 9, leaving medical cannabis's Schedule III classification intact and denying opponents had shown real harm.

Bipartisan senators revive SAFE Banking push — Sens. Merkley, Murkowski, Warren and Daines reintroduced the SAFE Banking Act of 2026 to give banks safe harbor serving cannabis businesses, with a House companion from Rep. Joyce and seven colleagues.

Trulieve becomes first plant-touching operator on the NYSE — Trulieve won approval to list under ticker TRLV, restructuring to a 100% medical footprint to clear the exchange's bar after federal Schedule III reclassification.

Congress races to save hemp before Nov. 12 ban — Reps. Barr and Craig's bipartisan Lawful Hemp Protection Act would swap the looming total ban for a regulated, tested, age-gated framework for hemp cannabinoid products.
